name: Kaluza-Klein Monopole
description: A static vacuum solution of gravity in five dimensions, four of space and one of time, that Rafael Sorkin, and David Gross and Malcolm Perry, found in 1983: Euclidean Taub-NUT space with a time added. The fifth dimension is a circle that shrinks smoothly to a point at the centre, and seen from four dimensions the twist of that circle is the field of a magnetic monopole.
convention: The length $m$ is the monopole's only parameter. We keep factors of $c$ explicit.
history: Theodor Kaluza wrote general relativity in five dimensions in 1921 and found Maxwell's equations inside it [kaluza1921, duff1994]. The components of the metric that mix the fifth dimension with the other four behave as the electromagnetic potential, which Michael Duff calls "the Kaluza miracle" [duff1994]. Oskar Klein answered in 1926 the question of why nobody had seen the fifth dimension: it is a circle, and a small one [klein1926, duff1994]. Duff's picture of it is a hosepipe, a line from far away and a little circle at every point from close up [duff1994].¶A magnetic monopole is allowed by quantum mechanics only if its charge $g$ and the electric charge $e$ satisfy $eg = n\hbar c/2$ for a whole number $n$, as Paul Dirac found in 1931 [dirac1931]. The vector potential of his monopole is singular along a line running out from it, the Dirac string [dirac1931]. Gravity has a magnetic charge of its own, the NUT parameter of the vacuum solution Ezra Newman, Louis Tamburino, and Theodore Unti published in 1963 [nut1963, lyndenbell1998]. Turn its time into a fourth direction of space and it becomes one of the gravitational instantons Stephen Hawking listed in 1977, the one whose curvature is self dual [hawking1977].¶Give Hawking's instanton a time and it becomes a magnetic monopole of Kaluza and Klein's theory, as Rafael Sorkin, and David Gross and Malcolm Perry, found in 1983 [sorkin1983, grossperry1983]. Sorkin added "the trivial term $-dt^2$" to the Euclidean line element of Newman, Unti, and Tamburino, and the result is a static solution of the vacuum Einstein equations in five dimensions [sorkin1983]. In Gross and Perry's coordinates it reads $$ds^2 = -c^2dt^2 + \left(1 + \frac{4m}{r}\right)\left(dr^2 + r^2d\Omega^2\right) + \left(1 + \frac{4m}{r}\right)^{-1}\left(dx_5 + 4m(1 - \cos\theta)\,d\phi\right)^2,$$ where the term mixing $x_5$ with $\phi$ is the potential of a monopole [grossperry1983, sen1997]. Seen from four dimensions the solution is a magnetic monopole obeying Dirac's quantisation condition [grossperry1983]. The point $r = 0$ is regular, and the Dirac string along $\theta = \pi$ is a coordinate singularity, provided $x_5$ is a circle of circumference $16\pi m$ [sen1997, gregory1997]. Far from the monopole that circle is Klein's hosepipe, and toward $r = 0$ the hose narrows until it closes [gregory1997].¶No matter went into the monopole, and Sorkin described it as "a perfectly regular five-geometry" that "appears singular from a four-dimensional perspective" [sorkin1983]. Push on it and it resists like a particle of mass around $m_P/e$, the Planck mass over the electric charge, which is Gross and Perry's estimate of its inertial mass [grossperry1983]. Set a slow test particle down beside it and the particle stays put: Gross and Perry found that the monopole exerts "no newtonian force on slowly moving test particles", so its gravitational mass is zero [grossperry1983]. They traced the inequality of the two masses to "the violation of Birkhoff's theorem in Kaluza-Klein theories" and found it consistent with the principle of equivalence [grossperry1983].¶Supergravity counts the monopoles as particles on the same footing as its own: in $N = 8$ supergravity in five dimensions they fill the same supermultiplets as the fields the theory starts with, as Gary Gibbons and Perry showed in 1984 [gibbonsperry1984]. A pair of monopoles moving slowly past each other feel no force at any separation, which Peter Ruback showed in 1986 [ruback1986]. The monopole's total energy took until 1987 to settle, when Luca Bombelli, Rabinder Koul, Gabor Kunstatter, Joohan Lee, and Sorkin computed it by three definitions of energy in five dimensions and showed that the three agree [bombelli1987].¶Type IIA string theory in ten dimensions is a theory in eleven with one dimension curled into a circle, Paul Townsend argued in 1995, and he interpreted its sixbranes "as the analogue of Kaluza-Klein monopoles" [townsend1995]. S-duality demands dyons, monopoles that also carry winding charge, and Ashoke Sen found in 1997 the zero modes that supply them, in the predicted number [sen1997]. Wind a string around the fifth dimension far from the monopole and it can come undone, as Ruth Gregory, Jeffrey Harvey, and Gregory Moore showed the same year [gregory1997]. Each surface of constant $t$ and $r$ is a squashed 3-sphere, on which every loop can be shrunk to a point, so the string slips off the hosepipe without ever going near the monopole [gregory1997]. Under T-duality, they noted, the Kaluza-Klein monopole becomes an H-monopole [gregory1997].

related.text: The monopole's four dimensions of space are Taub-NUT continued to Euclidean signature, in its self dual case and with NUT parameter $2m$. Sorkin made the monopole by giving that space a time [sorkin1983, hawking1977].

Rolled up to four dimensions, the monopole is the extreme magnetic black hole of Kaluza and Klein's theory, whose scalar field is a dilaton coupled with strength $\sqrt{3}$ where string theory's has strength $1$ [duff1994].

Any number of monopoles stay at rest wherever they are put, as Majumdar and Papapetrou's extremal black holes do, with $1 + \sum_i 4m/|\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{x}_i|$ in place of $1 + 4m/r$ [hawking1977, ruback1986].
A second static vacuum solution of gravity in five dimensions. Its 3-spheres are round and surround a horizon, and the monopole's are squashed and close smoothly at the nut.
Another vacuum solution of five dimensions with one direction rolled into a circle. Seen from four dimensions it is Schwarzschild's black hole, where the monopole is a magnetic charge [gregory2012].

A rotating black hole in five dimensions. With equal spins in its two planes each surface around it is a squashed 3-sphere as well, its Hopf circles stretched by the rotation where the monopole's shrink [emparan2008].
A fifth dimension of infinite size, with gravity held near a wall by the curvature of anti-de Sitter space [randall1999b].

coordinates.name: Gross-Perry

parameters.description: The monopole's one length: the fifth dimension has circumference $16\pi m$ far away

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi, x_5)$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time and the fifth coordinate $x_5$ a length, periodic with period $16\pi m$. The potential $A_\phi = 4m(1 - \cos\theta)$ vanishes on the half axis $\theta = 0$. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.

coordinates.name: Hopf Angle

parameters.description: The monopole's one length: the fifth dimension has circumference $16\pi m$ far away

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi, \psi)$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time and the angle $\psi = -\phi - x_5/4m$ periodic with period $4\pi$, so that $(\theta, \phi, \psi)$ are Euler angles on each 3-sphere of constant $t$ and $r$. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.

coordinates.name: Taub-NUT Radius

parameters.description: The monopole's one length: the fifth dimension has circumference $16\pi m$ far away

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, \rho, \theta, \phi, \psi)$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time, the radius $\rho = r + 2m$ of the Taub-NUT line element with NUT parameter $2m$, and the Euler angle $\psi$ periodic with period $4\pi$. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.
